tagline: Tick off your to-do list on a page, and trust what's left
use_when: You want to work through your project's to-do list by ticking items on a page, with finished work archived and anything claimed done actually checked first.
try_it: Use the todos skill to publish my open to-do items as a page I can tick off.

features.label: Your List, Tickable
features.sub: Open items from TODO.md become a page you tick off
features.title: Open items from TODO.md become a page you tick off
features.what: Your to-do file's open items are turned into a published page with a tick box and a note field for each. You work the list by clicking, not by editing a file.
features.html:
1. Renew the payment key   
2. Choose a tax setting
3. Add search to the blog

features.label: Five Clear Groups
features.sub: Items sit under Yours, Decide, Build, Backlog and Ongoing
features.title: Items sit under Yours, Decide, Build, Backlog and Ongoing
features.what: Every item belongs to one of five groups: things only you can do, decisions you owe, work Claude can build, later work, and long-running items. The group decides how a tick is handled afterward.
features.html:
Yours2
Decide1
Build4
Backlog6
Ongoing1

features.label: A Count You Can Trust
features.sub: Lines the page couldn't read are counted, not hidden
features.title: Lines the page couldn't read are counted, not hidden
features.what: The status bar reads like "18 open · 3 unparsed" when some lines in the file couldn't be read, and each one is named with its line number and the reason. A confident number never quietly drops real work.
features.html:
18 open · 3 unparsed
Line 42: finished item still in the list
Line 57: item outside any group

features.label: Copy From Anywhere
features.sub: The copy button stays on screen as you scroll
features.title: The copy button stays on screen as you scroll
features.what: Copy my replies sits in the pinned status bar as well as at the bottom, so on a phone you never scroll the whole list to find it.
features.html: 3 of 14 tickedCopy my replies

features.label: Done, But…
features.sub: Add a note to any item as you tick it
features.title: Add a note to any item as you tick it
features.what: Each item has an optional note, so an item can come back as "done, but the old key still works until Friday" rather than just a tick.
features.html:
1. Renew the payment key
done, old key works until Friday

features.label: Ticks Stay With Their Item
features.sub: Ticks and notes follow the item, not its position
features.title: Ticks and notes follow the item, not its position
features.what: Ticks and notes are saved against each item's title, not its number. When the list is renumbered, nothing slides onto the wrong item. Rewording an item clears its tick, since it is usually a new item.
features.html:
Renew the payment keywas #3, now #1
note keptsame item

features.label: Same Link, Ticks Kept
features.sub: The page updates at the link you already have
features.title: The page updates at the link you already have
features.what: The page is always republished to the same link, so your saved ticks and notes and your open tab stay put.
features.html: Monday→Fridaysame link

features.label: Your Word Is Final on Your Items
features.sub: Ticks on things only you can do are archived as-is
features.title: Ticks on things only you can do are archived as-is
features.what: A tick on a Yours or Decide item, like revoking a key or answering a question, can't be checked from the code, so it goes straight to the archive with your note.
features.html:
Yours · Renew key→ archived
Decide · Tax setting→ archived

features.label: Code Claims Get Checked
features.sub: Ticked build work is verified before it's archived
features.title: Ticked build work is verified before it's archived
features.what: A tick on Build, Backlog or Ongoing work starts a check against the actual code and history, like a matching commit, a file, a passing test or a merged change. Only what holds up gets archived, with the evidence.
features.html:
Build
Add search to the blog
commit found test passes change merged

features.label: Unproven Stays Open
features.sub: If the work isn't there, the item stays open with a note
features.title: If the work isn't there, the item stays open with a note
features.what: If the work isn't really there, the item stays on the list exactly where it was, with a dated note saying what was found. Nothing is archived on a tick alone.
features.html:
3. Add search to the blogStill open
Checked Nov 2: not on main, branch still open.

features.label: No Guessing on Matches
features.sub: If a reply could mean two items, you're asked which
features.title: If a reply could mean two items, you're asked which
features.what: Ticks are matched back to items by title. When a title could match more than one item, both are named and you choose, because archiving the wrong item can't be undone.
features.html:
"Update the key" matches two items:
1. Payment key5. Map key

features.label: Archived, Not Deleted
features.sub: Finished items move to a monthly archive with the evidence
features.title: Finished items move to a monthly archive with the evidence
features.what: Done items leave the live list for a monthly archive file, word for word, with the date, your note and what proved them done. The reasoning behind past work stays searchable.
features.html:
archive · this month
Renew the payment key
  archived: Nov 2

  evidence: ticked by you

features.label: Findings Aren't Tasks
features.sub: Notes and rules go to the docs, not the to-do list
features.title: Notes and rules go to the docs, not the to-do list
features.what: A root cause, a workaround or a standing rule is moved to the document that owns it instead of sitting in the list as fake work. What stays is real, open work.
features.html:
Workaround for slow builds→ project notes
Add search to the blogstays a task

features.label: Safe to Paste Twice
features.sub: Pasting the same reply again changes nothing
features.title: Pasting the same reply again changes nothing
features.what: Anything a reply names is already gone from the list after the first paste, so pasting it a second time is harmless.
features.html:
1st paste3 archived
2nd pastenothing to do

features.label: Tame an Overgrown List
features.sub: Turns a to-do file full of old history into a clean list
features.title: Turns a to-do file full of old history into a clean list
features.what: For a to-do file that has grown into a log of finished work, a one-time adopt step first reports how many items are done versus open before anything changes.
features.html:
Done214
Open19
Reported before anything moves

features.label: Open Items Checked First
features.sub: Every supposedly open item is checked against the code
features.title: Every supposedly open item is checked against the code
features.what: Before the list is rebuilt, each open item is checked to see whether it was quietly finished already. Items that turn out to be done go to the archive instead of staying on the list.
features.html:
19 open on paper
7 already built→ archive
12 really open→ list

features.label: History Moved Exactly
features.sub: Old entries move to monthly files, proven identical
features.title: Old entries move to monthly files, proven identical
features.what: Past entries are split into monthly archive files by their own dates, and every section is compared byte for byte before anything is written. If one doesn't match, nothing is written at all.
features.html: Oct matches Sep matches Aug matches

features.label: Every Move Explained
features.sub: You get a report of where each item went and why
features.title: You get a report of where each item went and why
features.what: The adopt step ends with a report of what was already built, what was really a note and moved to the docs, and which group each remaining item landed in.
features.html:
7 itemsalready built
3 itemsmoved to docs
12 itemssorted into groups

features.label: Where the Page Goes
features.sub: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.title: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.what: Your project picks where review pages go: a private claude.ai link, an HTML file that opens in your browser, or that file served on your home Wi-Fi so a phone can open it. Nothing is ever uploaded or tunneled in the Wi-Fi mode, and the server stops when the review ends.
